The competitive section faults Joern's 32-byte node records from before flatgraph (docs/overview.md:15-16). git log shows 147 of 154 commits by one author since 2026-08-08.
impact: Expert evaluators check claims first, and mismatches cost more trust than missing features. A bus factor of one also deters adopters and contributors.
recommendation: Keep a claims ledger that links each headline number to a benchmark artifact produced in CI, and label experimental features. Update the competitive section against current Joern, CodeQL and SootUp. Publish docs.rs API docs, a support matrix, ADRs, good-first issues and a discussion forum, and recruit co-maintainers.

title: No standard interop or query surface (SCIP/LSIF, a query language, LSP) and no stable symbol ids
evidence: QueryEngine offers just two hard-coded Rust calls, reachability and backward slice, and the u8 `query_type` field is not extensible. The CLI has only analyze, inspect, server and help. The LSPBridge, FileWatcher and didChange-to-SourceDelta pieces described in the docs do not exist. Entities are positional u32 sym_ids that change between builds, so cross-build diffs and external links are impossible.
impact: OpenHeart cannot plug into Sourcegraph, IDEs or CI, and users cannot write their own analyses. Joern (CPGQL), CodeQL (QL), Glean (Angle) and Kythe/SCIP all support this.
recommendation: Assign stable SCIP-style symbol strings or Kythe VNames, and export SCIP using the scip crate. Add a query layer, for example Datalog via ascent or crepe, a Trustfall adapter, or a Gremlin-like DSL. Add a tower-lsp server for definition, references and hover backed by TRA. Done means `scip lint` passes and an LSP smoke test works in VS Code.

title: Package, component and deployment views are containment counts with no dependency or build-metadata grounding
evidence: PackageRecord holds only class and subpackage counts, with no inter-package dependencies, although docs/uml_derivation.md:60 promises them. Components are exactly packages and `_cga` is unused. 'Provided' counts interfaces declared in the package, 'required' counts TH edges (duplicates included) to outside interfaces, and exporters render neither (bare boxes). Deployment reuses packages. No build or deployment metadata is read: pom.xml, build.gradle, module-info.java, DI annotations, Dockerfile or Kubernetes manifests.
impact: Architecture views carry no information beyond the directory tree, whereas Structure101, jQAssistant/ArchUnit-based views or Enterprise Architect show dependency structure, cycles and layering.
recommendation: Compute package dependency edges from type references and call edges, with cycle detection (Tarjan SCC) and Martin's metrics (Ca, Ce, I, A, D). Derive components from Maven/Gradle modules, JPMS modules and Spring @Component/@Service beans, with implemented interfaces as provided and injected interface-typed fields as required. Derive deployment from Dockerfile, compose, Kubernetes or Helm manifests, and mark it unavailable when they are absent.

title: Broken relative links and duplicated HTML docs
evidence: Across 32 Markdown files with 81 links (49 relative), 3 are broken. SUPPORT.md:32 points to ../README.md, outside the repo. SUPPORT.md:36 points to CONTRIBUTING.md, but the file is docs/contributing.md. examples/README.md:12 points to ./sample_project/, which does not exist. No heading anchors are broken. Five HTML docs are byte-identical copies in docs/ and web/docs/.
impact: New users hit dead links, and the duplicated docs will drift apart.
recommendation: Fix the three links. Add a link checker such as lychee to CI. Generate web/docs from docs/ during the Pages deploy.

title: A prompt written for an AI assistant is committed under docs/
evidence: docs/RESEARCH_PAPER_NEXT_PROMPT.txt:1 tells an assistant to make the paper 'undeniably unchallenged'. It sits next to docs/openheart_research_paper.tex and is not documentation.
impact: It suggests the claims were written to resist challenge rather than measured, which hurts credibility with benchmark reviewers.
recommendation: Remove the file. Back each claim in the paper with a script that reproduces it.

title: Competitor comparisons use unsourced figures that published data contradicts
evidence: docs/overview.md:16-25 asserts, without citations, that: Joern uses 32 B per node and 34 B per edge; EMF emits 100-150 MB per 1,000 classes; WALA/Soot need 8-16 GB per 1M LOC; and k=2 points-to runs out of memory above 500K LOC. overview.md:120 also compares against an uncited 170 MB Neo4j store. By contrast, Tai-e's paper (Table 1) reports Doop and Qilin finishing 2-obj on findbugs in 638 s and 2,033 s, and context-insensitive runs in 15-46 s.
impact: Unsourced claims of superiority invite rebuttal and erode trust in the rest of the documentation.
recommendation: Replace these with numbers the harness reproduces on the same corpus and hardware, or cite primary sources. Always label each number as 'published' or 'reproduced'.

title: Bitwise CRC-32 is duplicated and slow, and breaks the CRC-64 convention
evidence: src/scpg/serializer/integrity.rs:3-16 and src/tra/uml_link/hash_chain.rs:12-25 are identical bit-at-a-time CRC-32 loops (8 iterations per byte). The output is correct (0xCBF43926 for '123456789'). Every other artifact uses crc64_ecma, and README.md:59 says all phases produce 'CRC-64 verified binary artifacts'.
impact: There are two copies to maintain, and both run about 8x slower than a table-driven CRC on full-size sections.
recommendation: Keep one table-driven (or slicing-by-8) CRC in core and reuse it in TRA and SCPG. Either switch the .scpg sections to CRC-64 or correct the README.

title: Documented SCPG magic number disagrees with the constant, and the magic embeds a version
evidence: SCPG_MAGIC = u64::from_le_bytes(*b"SCPG\x00\x01\x00\x00") = 0x0000010047504353 (src/scpg/types.rs:3), but docs/plans/phase10.md:21 documents 0x5343504700010000. The mismatch error prints the little-endian value (src/scpg/mmap/mod.rs:30). The 0x01 byte in the magic duplicates format_version.
impact: Readers implemented from the spec reject valid files, and any version bump forces a change to the magic.
recommendation: Document the on-disk bytes ('SCPG\0\x01\0\0') rather than a u64 literal, print the magic as bytes in the error, and keep versioning in format_version only.

title: Per-function phases are sequential and never incremental
evidence: Phases 4 and 5 loop over functions sequentially, although each function is independent, and no parallelism crate is a dependency. There is no per-function fingerprint or cache: SSA ids are per-run positions and the call graph is rebuilt from scratch, while the incremental-sync doc promises to 'Recompute CFG, SSA, and ROBDD summaries only for affected functions'.
impact: Wall-clock time grows linearly with codebase size even for one-line edits, and extra cores sit idle.
recommendation: Use rayon par_iter over functions in Phases 4-5 with a deterministic merge order. Cache CFG and SSA per function, keyed by an AST-subtree hash. Update the call graph incrementally (re-resolve sites in changed methods plus a CHA delta), and use incremental dominator updates (Georgiadis et al.) for small edits.
